name: CA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 district partisanship in the Bay Area
No polls or expert ratings; challenger has minimal visible resources
model.rationale: The D+18 lean, DeSaulnier's incumbency, and his clear fundraising advantage over a little-funded challenger point to a Safe D race, and markets agree at roughly 96% for the incumbent. With no polls or ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much narrower margin or unexpected outside spending against DeSaulnier would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark DeSaulnier seeks another term in this heavily Democratic East Bay district, where the partisan lean is D+18. He enters the general with a large fundraising and cash-on-hand edge over Republican Jeff Frese, who reports no significant fundraising, and no outside spending is targeting the race.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, and prediction markets price DeSaulnier's chances near 96%. The combination of district partisanship, incumbency, and the money gap makes this a Safe Democratic seat with low uncertainty.
